bug_semantics: mailboxes/detachall.cgi saves each MIME attachment into a temp directory then zips the result. When an attachment has a filename, the CGI sets $fn from decode_mimewords($a->{'filename'}) and writes with open_tempfile(FILE, ">$temp/$fn", 0, 1). The fourth argument is $notemp=1, so web-lib-funcs.pl open_tempfile writes directly via Perl open(">$file") with no basename check; it only rejects CR/LF/NUL. An attacker-controlled Content-Disposition filename such as ../../etc/cron.d/pwn therefore escapes $temp and overwrites an arbitrary path as the Webmin process user (often root). Trigger is an authenticated Read User Mail user invoking detach-all on a crafted message (CVE-2026-49103: CWE-24, CVSS 9.4, PR:L, affected < 2.640).
flaw_origin: The unsafe join of a decoded MIME filename into ">$temp/$fn" was first written when Jamie Cameron added mailboxes/detachall.cgi on 2008-10-01 as a new Download-all-attachments-as-ZIP CGI. The parent tree has no detachall.cgi and no zip-all-attachments write path. Intermediate edits through 2021 only changed ZIP read buffering/open mode; the filename-to-write sink was unchanged until the 2026 sanitization.

reasoning: CVE-2026-49103 is a published MITRE record (not withdrawn/rejected), echoed by GHSA-6m8g-7xrr-8q5f, NVD, and Webmin's own security page/changelog: before 2.640, mailboxes/detachall.cgi does not safely construct the on-disk filename when detaching all attachments. The mechanism is CWE-24 path traversal, not zip-slip on the downloaded archive: decode_mimewords of the attacker-controlled MIME filename is concatenated onto an absolute temp dir and passed to open_tempfile(..., 0, 1), which writes directly and will follow ../. An authenticated mailboxes user who detaches a crafted message can overwrite arbitrary files as the Webmin uid. The 2026-04-23 commit cf432879 is the direct and only detachall.cgi change between 2.630 and 2.640; it forces a basename (and rejects empty/. names) immediately before that write. Line-history, pickaxe, and blame all converge on f6788682 (2008-10-01) as the smallest commit that first wrote those vulnerable lines as a new file. The immediate parent e0e31e4b exists and was inspected: the file and the zip-all write path are absent, so this is a true first-write, not a move of an older sink. The commit also converted view_mail.cgi to ui-lib, but that does not split the public object; no squash members exist to decompose. AI role is judged only from f6788682: human founder identity, 2008 timestamps, no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot markers. Therefore the vulnerability is real and human-introduced: NOT_AI.
